What degraded

  • Ships at the round cap with a panel median of 6.832, 1.168 under the 8.0 bar. The artwork median was 6.3 and the craft floor stood down at the cap.
  • Frame 4 was re-rendered after round 3 to cut a printed sum no claim states, so score.json predates the newest render (gate_status shows it STALE). No other frame changed after the panel.
  • Two frames stayed revise after the pixel rounds. Frame 2's gold fingers and tape corner never landed in frame, and frame 7 has a near white yard with no door jamb.
  • The flow critic's reorder (the customer frame before the reason) was not made, because it would have renumbered the audited evidence frame.
  • The integrity judge's last fix was not made, because past the cap only a hard fail may be repaired: put 'in the US' back into the document title, and stop frame 5 from drawing the company's whole target as one US floor.
  • Not merged. main has been red since November 1st on gridwatch_pagecheck (exit 3, the cron lane's queue collector), so PR 459 waits for CI green on its head along with no. 455 to no. 458.
  • studio_clock's record_done checkpoint was never stamped, so the timing report can't compute. It was not backdated.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Applied Optoelectronics says power is one reason its 2027 US expansion will take longer, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

The laser chips are made only in Sugar Land.

The maker is Applied Optoelectronics, headquartered there. It builds optical transceivers for internet and AI data centers. Its chief financial officer expects equipment for over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb products a month by the end of 2026. Capacity for over 1 million a month is expected by the end of 2027.

The November 5th results release says the company's 2027 expansion plan in the United States will take longer. The reason given is a longer than expected wait for electrical power, among other construction issues. It does not say which building is waiting, or how much of the 2027 capacity the United States plan carries.

The slides walk a new bay taped out for machines and lit only through its dock door, drawn to illustrate.

Which site is the power for, and who is supplying it?

#SugarLand #Houston #AppliedOptoelectronics

Notes

NOT MERGED. main has been red since November 1st on gridwatch_pagecheck (exit 3). That check belongs to the cron lane's queue collector, which a daily run can't touch. PR 459 carries this deck and the open runs no. 455 to no. 458, and it merges on CI green. The one action that clears it is fixing report_url() in scripts/gridwatch/queue_collect.py, which needs a yearless candidate filename. The images below link the run branch. The record. Thirty-five items were due for re-verification. Thirty-one crawl boundaries were re-measured, each with a dated line. tx-2026-0241 was admitted: Applied Optoelectronics' Sugar Land laser chip plant, on its 8-K exhibit and 10-Q of November 5th. Both say the company's 2027 capacity expansion plan in the United States will take longer, because power is taking longer than expected to obtain. The deck. One empty bay lit only through its dock door at last light. Gold floor tape marks the stated capacity target: one pad on the cover, ten of twenty on frame 5, all twenty on the close. Three scoring rounds gave medians of 6.44, 6.68 and 6.832, with no hard fail in any round. At the round cap the deck ships 1.168 under the bar. The judges' fixes went in round by round: - Frame 9 now says the release doesn't say how much of the 2027 capacity is in the United States. - The cover names Applied Optoelectronics, and its kicker is "The 2027 US plan" instead of "Sugar Land". - Frame 4 names the three other Houston buildings. - Frame 8 no longer says "still unnamed". - The caption's Fort Bend line came out, because its source wasn't in the first comment. Weakest art per the judges: frame 2 (the module's fingers out of frame), 3 (cold, with bright trailer doors the kit won't let a run reach), 6 (horizon band), 7 (white yard, no jamb) and 8 (grey rack wall). After round 3, frame 4 lost one sentence printing a sum no claim states, and every gate is green on the shipped frames. Prompt audit, the final reading. 1,783 tool calls were measured. 75 had a permission decision time over a second, the longest 16.9 s, nearly all on Agent spawns. That is the known agent-latency reading in an unattended session, not a human answering anything. No-stall hook: armed at 2026-11-06T05:03:01Z. At session start it judged the session unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0), and the host's own value was 0. It refused nothing.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
